question.worked_solution:
We proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{-2}\frac{5}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x & =5{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{-2}\frac{1}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[-\frac{1}{4{x}^{4}}]}_{a}^{-2} \\  & =-\frac{5}{4}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}]}_{a}^{-2} \\  & =-\frac{5}{4}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }[\frac{1}{(-2)^{4}}-\frac{1}{{a}^{4}}] \\  & =-\frac{5}{4}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }(\frac{1}{16}-\frac{1}{{a}^{4}}) \\  & =-\frac{5}{4}(\frac{1}{16}-0) \\  & =-\frac{5}{64}.\end{aligned}
$$
